stops.name: Manchester Cathedral
stops.shortDescription: The historic starting point of the city. Originally a collegiate church dating back to 1421, it features some of the finest late-medieval woodwork in the North of England.

stops.name: Chetham's Library
stops.shortDescription: Founded in 1653, this incredibly atmospheric building is the oldest surviving public library in the English-speaking world. Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels famously studied together here.

stops.name: National Football Museum
stops.shortDescription: Housed in the striking, modern glass Urbis building, this museum celebrates the history and culture of the beautiful game, housing over 140,000 football-related objects.

stops.name: Afflecks
stops.shortDescription: A legendary indoor market spreading across four floors. It defines the independent, alternative spirit of the Northern Quarter, packed with vintage clothes, records, and quirky boutiques.

stops.name: Stevenson Square
stops.shortDescription: The historic heart of the bohemian Northern Quarter. It is famous for its vibrant, ever-changing street art that often covers the walls and old public toilet blocks.

stops.name: Chinatown Arch
stops.shortDescription: The second largest Chinatown in the UK. The entrance is marked by a magnificent, highly decorated traditional Chinese paifang arch, originally built in China and shipped over in pieces.

stops.name: Manchester Art Gallery
stops.shortDescription: Housed in a grand neoclassical building designed by Charles Barry. The gallery is internationally renowned for its outstanding, world-class collection of Pre-Raphaelite paintings.

stops.name: St Peter's Square & Central Library
stops.shortDescription: A sweeping, recently redesigned civic square dominated by the Central Library. The library's breathtaking, Pantheon-inspired circular design makes it an architectural icon of the city.

stops.name: Manchester Town Hall
stops.shortDescription: An absolute masterpiece of Victorian neo-Gothic architecture dominating Albert Square. Its towering clock tower stands as a proud symbol of the city's vast wealth during the Industrial Revolution.

stops.name: St Ann's Square
stops.shortDescription: A historic, elegant pedestrianized square known for the 18th-century St Ann's Church. Today, it serves as one of the city's most upscale and relaxing shopping areas.

stops.name: Royal Exchange Theatre
stops.shortDescription: A truly unique theatrical space. A futuristic, lunar-module-like glass theatre is suspended directly inside the massive, opulent grand hall of the former Cotton Exchange.

stops.name: Barton Arcade
stops.shortDescription: A stunning, beautifully restored Victorian shopping arcade. It is constructed almost entirely of intricately detailed cast iron and glass, offering a glimpse into 19th-century luxury.

stops.name: John Rylands Library
stops.shortDescription: A breathtaking neo-Gothic library standing proudly on Deansgate. Its vaulted ceilings and quiet, cathedral-like historic reading room feel like stepping straight out of a fantasy novel.

stops.name: Great Northern Warehouse
stops.shortDescription: A massive, imposing Victorian goods warehouse that powerfully represents the city's industrial past. It has now been transformed into a bustling leisure and dining complex.

stops.name: Mamucium (Roman Fort)
stops.shortDescription: The reconstructed ruins of the original Roman fort dating back to 79 AD. It is literally the historical birthplace where the ancient settlement of Manchester first began.

stops.name: Castlefield Canals
stops.shortDescription: The picturesque terminus of the Bridgewater Canal, the world's first industrial canal. The area is defined by its massive, intersecting red-brick railway viaducts and relaxing waterside pubs.
